fullPassage:
Over time, certain biological and behavioral features of humans stop serving a purpose. Instead of disappearing completely, they remain intact but have no function. This is what happened with the grasp reflex. If you place an object in an infant's hand, he or she will automatically grab it. This reflex was helpful for our distant ancestors, whose babies had to hold tightly to their mothers' fur. But the grasp reflex is of little use to human babies now, as they don't have to cling for survival. Another unnecessary feature we inherited from our ancestors is goose bumps. Goose bumps occur when we are cold or frightened and the hairs on our body stand straight up. Today, they are anything but useful. But they kept our hairy ancestors warm because the erect hairs prevented body heat from escaping. They also made our ancestors appear larger, helping them scare away predators.

The iris is a muscle found in the eye. It can control the amount of light that enters the eye by opening and closing the pupil. Each of a person's two irises has a pattern of textures which is different from that of the other, as these patterns are not genetic. DNA decides the color and structure of the iris, but the patterns are formed randomly while the baby is still developing in the womb. As the baby opens and closes its eyes, the tissue of the iris moves and folds, creating patterns. Like fingerprints, iris patterns are unique and rarely change over time, so they are now often used for identification.

Dear Staff and Supporters, Our plan to move our bird exhibits to a larger space was intended to enhance the quality of the birds' lives. However, we have decided that our planned move is not necessarily a good idea at the present time. In-depth discussions with experts have led us to believe that the move could produce dangerous levels of stress as well as potential health risks for the birds. Not every member of the zoo's board of directors agreed, but we have decided to cancel the move. While this is not quite the outcome we had hoped for, we will continue to seek out other ways of improving our bird exhibits. Thank you for your understanding and support. Sincerely, Zoo Manager

In the 15th century, some Europeans used a strange medicine to stay healthy. It was called "mumia," and it was made from ground-up mummies. People ate it or rubbed it into injuries. They believed it could be used to treat coughs and headaches. However, mumia was not always embraced by the medical community. Additionally, not all patients were willing to try it. Despite this, there was still a high demand for mumia in Europe. Some people dug up Egyptian graves to steal the mummies. Others attempted to turn the bodies of people who had recently died into mummies. Modern people would view this practice as a kind of cannibalism. Medieval Europeans, however, considered it an unusual type of medicine. Fortunately, as medical knowledge advanced, doctors eventually stopped prescribing mumia.

A parasocial relationship occurs when an individual invests emotional energy, interest, and time in someone who is unaware of their existence. Commonly seen with fans of celebrities, these one-sided relationships allow individuals to attach themselves without the fear of disapproval or rejection. Even if there is no chance of a real interaction, studies indicate that these chosen relationships offer companionship and emotional support, especially during difficult times. These relationships are by no means meaningless because they have been shown to play a role in shaping an individual's personal identity. There is no doubt at all that parasocial relationships can hold significant value in enriching one's life.

Before the 16th century, there were no sizing systems for clothing whatsoever. Then, in 1589, one of the first written works related to the tailoring of clothes was published. This may have represented the beginnings of modern measurement standards. At the start of the 19th century, however, clothes were still being measured individually. It was a series of wars that finally led to the establishment of universal sizing, due to a sudden increase in the demand for military uniforms. By the end of the century, men's clothing was being sold in standardized sizes that didn't require any additional measurements. Women's clothing, however, took longer to change, as it was generally much more close-fitting. It wasn't until the early 20th century that ready-to-wear women's clothing became popular.

det.analysis:
① happened: 'This is what happened with the grasp reflex'는 과거에 일어난 일이라 과거동사 happened가 맞아요. 적절합니다.

② inherited: 'feature we inherited from our ancestors'는 '우리가 물려받은 특징'이라는 과거의 일이라 과거동사 inherited가 맞아요. 적절합니다.

③ prevented: 'the erect hairs prevented body heat'는 '막았다'는 과거의 일이라 과거동사 prevented가 맞아요. 적절합니다.

④ helping: 'They also made our ancestors appear larger, ___ them scare away predators'를 보세요. 이미 앞에 'made'라는 본동사가 있고, 두 문장을 잇는 접속사(and 등)가 없어요. 이럴 때 '그래서 ~하며'라는 뜻을 더하려면 동사에 -ing를 붙인 분사구문 helping을 써야 해요. helped(과거동사)를 쓰면 접속사 없이 동사가 둘이 되어 문장이 깨져요. ←정답
det.tip: 접속사 없이 동사를 하나 더 이으려면 분사구문(-ing). 콤마 뒤 helping(O) / helped(X)

④ identification(신원 확인): 홍채 무늬가 신원 확인에 쓰임 — 적절
det.tip: DNA가 색·구조를 decides(결정). ignores(무시)는 반대

questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① 불일치 — 상대가 개인의 존재를 모르는 '일방적(one-sided)' 관계라고 했어요. 서로 주고받는 쌍방향이 아니에요.

❌ ② 불일치 — '실제 상호작용의 가능성이 없어도(no chance of a real interaction)' 성립한다고 했어요. 실제로 만난 적이 있어야 하는 게 아니에요.

❌ ③ 불일치 — '정체성을 형성하는 데 역할을 한다(play a role in shaping ~ identity)'고 했으니 영향을 미쳐요.

✅ ④ 일치 — 'someone who is unaware of their existence(그 개인의 존재를 알지 못하는 사람)'와 정확히 맞아요 ←정답
det.tip: 핵심 = 상대는 팬의 존재도 모름(일방적). 그래서 ④가 일치예요.

ch: 준사회적 관계는 양측이 서로 감정을 주고받는 쌍방향 관계다.

questions.passage: Before the 16th century, there ①<u>were</u> no sizing systems for clothing whatsoever. Then, in 1589, one of the first written works related to the tailoring of clothes was ②<u>published</u>. This may have ③<u>representing</u> the beginnings of modern measurement standards. At the start of the 19th century, however, clothes were still being measured individually. It was a series of wars that finally led to the establishment of universal sizing, due to a sudden increase in the demand for military uniforms. By the end of the century, men's clothing was being sold in standardized sizes that didn't ④<u>require</u> any additional measurements. Women's clothing, however, took longer to change, as it was generally much more close-fitting. It wasn't until the early 20th century that ready-to-wear women's clothing became popular.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: representing → represented (may have + 과거분사)
det.analysis:
① were: 'there ___ no sizing systems'의 주어는 복수명사 systems라 were가 맞아요 — 적절.

② published: 'was published'는 be동사 + 과거분사의 수동태예요 — 적절.

③ representing: 'This may have ___ the beginnings'에서 may have 뒤에는 과거분사가 와야 해요(may/might + have + p.p. = 과거에 대한 추측). 현재분사 representing이 아니라 과거분사 represented가 맞아요. ←정답

④ require: 'didn't require'는 조동사 did 뒤 동사원형이라 — 적절.
det.tip: may/might + have + 과거분사 = ~했을지도 모른다(과거 추측). may have represented

questions.passage: The iris is a muscle found in the eye. It can control the amount of light that ①<u>enter</u> the eye by opening and closing the pupil. Each of a person's two irises ②<u>has</u> a pattern of textures which is different from that of the other, as these patterns are not genetic. DNA decides the color and structure of the iris, but the patterns are ③<u>formed</u> randomly while the baby is still developing in the womb. As the baby opens and closes its eyes, the tissue of the iris moves and folds, creating patterns. Like fingerprints, iris patterns are unique and rarely change over time, so they are now often ④<u>used</u> for identification.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: enter → enters (that의 선행사 light가 단수·불가산이므로 단수동사 enters)
det.analysis:
① enter: 'the amount of light that enter the eye'? 관계대명사 that의 선행사는 light(단수·불가산)라서 동사도 단수형 enters가 와야 해요. enter는 틀리므로 enters로 고쳐야 해요 ←정답

② has: 'Each of ~ irises has'에서 주어의 핵심은 Each(단수)라 단수동사 has — 적절

③ formed: 'the patterns are formed randomly'에서 무늬가 형성되는 수동태 be+과거분사 — 적절

④ used: 'they are ~ used for identification'에서 be+과거분사 수동태 — 적절
det.tip: 관계대명사절 동사는 선행사에 일치: light(단수) → enters

questions.passage: The iris is a muscle found in the eye. It can control the amount of light that enters the eye by opening and closing the pupil. questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 본문 첫 두 문장 'The iris is a muscle found in the eye. It can control the amount of light'과 일치하는 것은 ②예요.
det.analysis:
① 부모에게서 유전: 무늬는 유전적이지 않다(not genetic)고 했으므로 불일치

② 눈 속 근육으로 빛의 양 조절: 본문 첫 두 문장과 일치 ←정답

③ DNA가 무늬를 무작위로 생성: DNA는 색과 구조만 결정하고 무늬는 무작위로 형성 — 불일치

④ 시간이 지나면 쉽게 바뀜: 좀처럼 변하지 않는다(rarely change)고 했으므로 불일치
det.tip: 홍채 = 눈 속 근육 + 빛의 양 조절(첫 두 문장)

ch: 홍채는 눈 속에 있는 근육으로 빛의 양을 조절한다.
DNA가 홍채의 무늬를 무작위로 만들어 낸다.
홍채 무늬는 시간이 지나면 쉽게 바뀐다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: improve → improving (전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사가 오므로 improve가 아니라 improving)
det.analysis:

② produce: 'the move could produce'에서 조동사 could 뒤에는 동사원형이 와요. 그래서 produce가 맞아요 — 적절

③ cancel: 'decided to cancel'에서 to 뒤에는 동사원형이 오므로 cancel이 맞아요 — 적절

④ improve: 'other ways of improve'처럼 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 와야 해요. 그래서 improve가 아니라 improving이 맞습니다 ←정답
det.tip: 전치사(of) 뒤에는 동명사(-ing) → ways of improving

questions.passage: In the 15th century, some Europeans used a strange medicine to stay healthy. It was called "mumia," and it was made from ground-up mummies. People ate it or rubbed it into injuries. They believed it could be used __________. However, mumia was not always embraced by the medical community. Others attempted to turn the bodies of people who had recently died into mummies. Modern people would view this practice as a kind of cannibalism. ③ to preserve dead bodies longer: '시신 보존'은 약의 복용 목적과 무관 — 오답

questions.passage: Over time, certain biological and behavioral features of humans stop serving a purpose. Instead of disappearing completely, they remain intact but have no function. This is what happened with the grasp reflex. If you place an object in an infant's hand, he or she will automatically grab it. This reflex was helpful for our distant ancestors, whose babies had to hold tightly to their mothers' fur. But the grasp reflex is of little use to human babies now, as they don't have to cling for survival. Another unnecessary feature we inherited from our ancestors is goose bumps. Goose bumps occur when we are cold or frightened and the hairs on our body stand straight up. Today, they are anything but useful. But they kept our hairy ancestors warm because the erect hairs prevented body heat from escaping. They also made our ancestors __________, helping them scare away predators.
